findings.title: Pages below the homepage carry no breadcrumb markup
findings.evidence: 20 of 20 sampled non-homepage pages have no BreadcrumbList markup. Examples: https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/art_25/index.html.

evidence_detail.method: presence of a BreadcrumbList node, after full @graph traversal, on pages other than the homepage
evidence_detail.expected: BreadcrumbList markup below the homepage, where the site has a real hierarchy

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList markup reflecting each page's position in the site hierarchy.
how: Generate it from the same navigation hierarchy the template already renders as a visible breadcrumb, if one exists.
Each ListItem needs position, name and item (the URL).
suggested_action.mechanism: Breadcrumb markup gives a machine an explicit statement of where a page sits in the site's structure, which is otherwise only inferable from the URL path.
suggested_action.verification: Re-check the page and confirm BreadcrumbList markup parses and matches the page's actual position.

findings.title: The homepage declares no organization or local-business entity
findings.evidence: The homepage (https://books.toscrape.com/) has no Organization, LocalBusiness or equivalent entity in its JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa, after traversing any @graph fully. There is no explicit machine-readable statement of which brand this site belongs to.

evidence_detail.method: JSON-LD @graph traversal, Microdata itemtype and RDFa typeof checked for an Organization, LocalBusiness or Corporation node on the homepage
evidence_detail.expected: an Organization or LocalBusiness node on the homepage

suggested_action.summary: Add one Organization (or LocalBusiness, if there is a physical location) node to the homepage, in JSON-LD, with a stable identifier.
how: Include at minimum name, url, and logo.
Give it an @id so other structured data on the site can reference it rather than duplicating it.
Add sameAs links to profiles the brand actually controls.
suggested_action.mechanism: This is the single node a system uses to resolve 'this site' into 'this real-world brand'. Without it, every other page's content is attributed to an inferred entity rather than a declared one.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the homepage and confirm an Organization node with a name and url parses successfully.

findings.title: No structured data of any kind was found on the sampled pages
findings.evidence: None of the 21 sampled content pages carry JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa. A machine can read the text but has no explicit signal for what kind of thing each page describes or which entity it belongs to.

evidence_detail.method: presence of any parseable JSON-LD, Microdata itemtype or RDFa typeof, checked across every sampled content page
evidence_detail.expected: at least some structured data, of any of the three formats

suggested_action.summary: Add structured data for at least the organisation identity and the page types this site actually has, in JSON-LD.
how: Start with an Organization node on the homepage.
Add the type each template warrants: Product for product pages, Article for editorial content, and so on.
JSON-LD in a single script block in the page head is the easiest to maintain and validate.
suggested_action.mechanism: Structured data lets a machine classify content and resolve which real-world entity a page is about, without inferring it from prose. Its absence does not block reading the page, but it leaves classification to inference, which is less reliable.
suggested_action.verification: Run the page through a structured-data validator and confirm at least one recognised type is detected.
